transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-30
Start time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim, Priya Nair, Marcus Li, Aisha Gomez, Tom Reed, Emily Zhang, Ben Carver

Summary: internal enablement; messy transcript with natural talk patterns and some auto-transcribe errors

00:00 Jordan: okay hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll get started in a minute, um this is the SE enablement session on messaging and demo practice, we wanted to run through the new Dedicated vs Hosted narrative and practice the demo flows, also refine the battle card language for competitors, uh a quick check everyone good audio?
00:12 Priya: yeah sounds good Jordan, loud and clear, I'll take notes on the competitive bits
00:15 Marcus: yep, good here, planning to demo the throughput dashboard then run the small-batch example
00:22 Aisha: hi all, just want to surface a new customer quote from the marketing side that might be useful: "saved 37% token cost month one with intelligent batching" — not final wording
00:34 Tom: quick ask from sales mgmt — we need clearer callouts on when to push Dedicated vs Hosted during discovery, timing matters
00:42 Jordan: yes, that's one of our main goals today, to make that decision tree tactile for AEs
00:50 Emily: curious if we have an updated line on Private deployments for regulated customers, like data residency plus KMS details?
00:58 Priya: short answer: Private (VPC/on-prem) supports customer-managed KMS, audit logs, and we can do on-prem packages for air-gapped — but we should not overpromise latency parity, ok?
01:12 Jordan: right, and put that in the slide: "Private for max control + compliance" then list tradeoffs

02:05 Marcus: okay demo plan — I'll start with the Redwood Console overview, quick perf dashboard, then spin up the Dedicated pool example and show the autoscaling trigger at 70% GPU util, then fall back to hosted variant to show graceful degradation
02:20 Priya: nice, remember to call out KV cache and prefix caching as a cost/latency lever, people miss that often
02:30 Jordan: maybe we role-play a customer objection: "Your Dedicated pricing is too high compared to hosted or other vendors" — how do we answer?
02:42 Tom: standard answer is drive to unit economics: show tokens per second, latency SLOs, predictability of throughput; point to reserved discount versus burst pricing
02:55 Priya: and emphasize operational overhead — other vendors have hidden ops costs if you self-host, but don't slam open source, just position the risk/obs
03:12 Marcus: i sometimes say — "you can run on your infra but you lose our autoscaling, tracing, and rollout protection" — keeps it factual
03:25 Emily: what about comparisons to OpenAI? AEs ask if we compete on model capability or just infra
03:33 Priya: clarify: we're not a model vendor — we provide serving and ops, we host curated models and have Redwood-verified performance. So the framing is: "we make model serving predictable and economical"
03:45 Jordan: good, say that and then show the console metrics so they see the economics live

04:10 Ben: question — on the security talking points, do we have an up-to-date list of certs? SOC2, ISO? Also SSO/SAML examples?
04:20 Priya: yes SOC 2 Type II in our standard package, ISO in progress — for demos say: "SOC 2, SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integrations available". add nuance on Private: can do on-prem + HSM
04:36 Jordan: note: don't say "FIPS" unless confirmed; marketing will check the compliance page before publishing

05:00 Marcus: starting demo practice — I'll be the SE, Jordan you'll be the AE/customer combined — emulate a mid-market customer concerned about latency and cost
05:12 Jordan: sure, i'm "CE0 of AcmePlex" — uh sorry CEO — and I want low latency for chat and tight cost controls
05:20 Marcus: so I share screen — open console, model catalog, show a curated model "rw-alpha-13b-8k" (transcript: model name may be garbled in auto-transcribe), then show per-token latency plot
05:36 Marcus: here's our throughput line, you can see DP reserved pool at 95% util earlier but avg latency 70 ms for 512 tokens, now show what happens when we enable quantization + batching
05:52 Jordan: interrupting — people will ask "can you get to 20ms?" what's honest answer
05:58 Priya: depends on model/seq length/hardware; 20ms is possible for small single-turn prompts on optimized kernels and shorter sequences, but don't promise 20ms for all production chat with long KV caches
06:12 Tom: sellers often oversell that. Good to offer a benchmark: "we can run a targeted benchmark in your environment within 2 weeks" and propose a POC with metrics

06:40 Marcus: now demo the fallback — simulate Dedicated pool saturating, the smart router automatically shifts new requests to hosted with compatible model variant; show the request trace and the replica id, trace shows fallbacks and no errors
06:55 Jordan: nice visual. For messaging: highlight the resilience story — "we keep you live, with predictable cost tiers"
07:06 Priya: also note the routing policy options: latency-first, cost-first, region priority. That's a key differentiation versus naive single-endpoint offerings

07:40 Emily: short roleplay — I'm skeptical about lock-in if I move to Redwood Dedicated, people ask how hard is it to change models or leave
07:52 Marcus: answer: our model catalog promotes open models, you can export model artifacts and we support standard formats; emphasize data portability + model versioning + rollout tools. Again avoid absolute statements about all custom infra
08:10 Jordan: add a line about migration support and playbooks we provide — helps reassure

08:30 Priya: on the competitive card — for Anthropic the angle is safety and instruction tuning; for Hugging Face it's open model ecosystem and community; for OpenAI it's brand + model research. Our sweet spot: serving, ops, cost controls, and enterprise features
08:50 Aisha: marketing wants one-liners for each competitor — can you draft two-sentence positioning for the enablement one-pager?
08:58 Priya: yes I'll do that, draft to include strengths + where we win and where to avoid fights (e.g., we don't beat OpenAI on family of proprietary models)

09:20 Marcus: back to demo practice — hands-on quick commands: show batch size toggles, quantization flags, and the kernel selection note — the console exposes optimized kernel hints but you can also pass flags in the config
09:40 Jordan: small nit — remember customers rarely want deep infra commands in demo; show high-level toggles then offer a technical deep-dive if they want more
09:52 Emily: can we capture a short script for AEs — three bullets: 1) discovery questions, 2) recommended demo path, 3) common objection answers
10:05 Ben: i can make the one-pager, Marcus will give me the demo commands list to embed as an appendix

10:20 Tom: a tricky objection: "Your claimed cost savings rely on caching and batching but we can't guarantee savings with our traffic profile" how to respond
10:32 Priya: respond with data: ask about seq length, concurrency, cold vs warm starts; offer to run a trace-level benchmark or baseline sample using their prompt set; show percent breakdown by token consumption and batching impact
10:50 Marcus: and mention we have Optimize recommendations: model/quantization suggestions per workload — that's a soft product plug

11:05 Jordan: role play time — Emily you ask the latency-cost question and then we'll demo the autoscale rule and manual override
11:12 Emily: okay, as a customer, "I need 99th percentile under 200ms, but our cost target is X" — what's the quick pitch?
11:24 Marcus: show autoscale, show dedicated throughput, then show how to configure routing policy to prefer Dedicated at low cost but fallback to hosted on overload. point to SLA + cost model in console
11:40 Priya: also mention we provide cost-allocation by token and route-level cost views — helps product managers justify spend

12:05 Jordan: good, good — interrupting: we should rehearse the opening lines for the demo: quick context, what success looks like, and 2-min console tour; keep it under 8 minutes before Q&A
12:20 Ben: i'll put that into the demo checklist — intro, perf slide, live demo, canary/rollback, Q&A

12:40 Aisha: folks, on messaging tone — we prefer "production-first" not "enterprise-first" in the new copy, because we want to speak to startups too
12:50 Priya: agreed, replace enterprise-first with production-first in the deck headers

13:05 Jordan: OK last block — competitive rebuttals practice, I'll read one and you respond as if on a sales call
13:12 Jordan: "We can get lower cost with self-hosting on spot instances"
13:18 Priya: "You might save on raw infra, but you incur ops, monitoring, reliability and SLO maintenance costs — we quantify that with per-token latency and failure reduction metrics"
13:30 Marcus: add: "And we provide rollout policies and canarying that avoid customer-visible regressions, that's often the hidden cost of self-hosting"

13:45 Jordan: final recap — key takeaways: update battle card, record short demo snippets, create AE script and checklist, run targeted benchmarks for large deals. Next steps and owners are captured in action items
13:55 Tom: i'll follow up with scheduling for 1:1 demo shadows and prioritize which AEs to train first
14:02 Jordan: thanks everyone, end

Notes: transcription has some minor auto-transcribe errors in model names and acronyms, occasional speaker attribution mix-ups; audio overlaps during fast exchanges.
